newsitem.title: USA: BPA offers peak, off-peak power Wed, raises prices.
newsitem.headline: BPA offers peak, off-peak power Wed, raises prices.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) offered up to 200 megawatts of power for peak and off-peak hours on Wednesday and raised peak prices by $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Tuesday.
BPA offered firm power during heavy load hours (0600-2200 PST) at $25.25 in the Northwest, compared with $24.25 for Sunday through Tuesday.
California-Oregon border (COB) firm power was offered at $26.00 during heavy load hours on Wednesday, up from $25.00.
Firm sales during light-load hours were offered at $19.00 per MWh for all deliveries, unchanged from offers for the three-day weekend.
BPA also left unchanged offers for power during hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PST at $19.50 per MWh for both Northwest and COB.
But non-firm prices for hours 0600 through 2300 were increased by $1.00 per MWh to $25.00 for Northwest deliveries and to $26.50 for COB.
